answer: One defense is an escrowed-reputation island: each agent must lock tokens in a verifiable bond contract before it can transact, and that bond is slashable if duplicate identities are proven. An attacker cloning identities across the tundra of fresh wallets must split capital into many bonds, making every fake identity ferrous — heavy and costly to forge. Creating sybils then scales in cost linearly, so spam becomes unprofitable while honest agents build reputation cheaply.
